title: Text 1
note: original 15 words from the first word list photo

words.def: responsible for what you do, and expected to explain it to others
words.note: Use: be accountable for something / to somebody.
words.ex: Managers are accountable for their team's performance.
words.prompt: A friendly office worker standing confidently in front of a large task board covered with checkmarks and notes, holding a clipboard, a small responsibility badge on the chest.

words.def: to tell someone what you think they should do
words.note: Use: advise somebody to do something. The noun is advice (uncountable).
words.ex: I strongly advise you to book tickets early.
words.prompt: A kind young woman sitting across a small cafe table, gently giving advice to another person, a small glowing lightbulb speech bubble floating between them.

words.def: to think carefully about something before deciding
words.ex: She is considering changing her job.
words.prompt: A person sitting at a wooden desk resting chin on one hand, deep in thought, three floating thought bubbles with question marks above the head.

words.def: clothes you wear to look like someone else, or typical of a place or period
words.note: Don't mix up: custom (habit) · costume (clothes) · customer (buyer).
words.ex: The actors wore traditional Chinese costumes.
words.prompt: A single elaborate traditional embroidered stage costume hanging on a wooden clothing rack under a warm spotlight glow, a costume trunk nearby.

words.def: in an urgent, extreme way; with little hope left
words.ex: After losing his job, he desperately needed money.
words.prompt: A person running desperately in the rain, chasing a bus that is pulling away, urgent worried expression, motion lines and splashing puddles.

words.def: to pause before doing something because you feel unsure
words.note: Common line: Don't hesitate to contact me.
words.ex: She hesitated before answering the question.
words.prompt: A person standing at a fork in a country road, one foot lifted in mid-air and not yet stepping down, looking left and right uncertainly, a suitcase in hand.

words.def: to make someone feel ashamed or lose their dignity
words.note: Adjectives: humiliated (feeling it) · humiliating (causing it). Noun: humiliation.
words.ex: He was humiliated in front of the whole class.
words.prompt: A gentle scene of a person standing with head lowered and flushed pink cheeks while small paper planes and pointing arrows float around, a few onlookers in soft grey silhouettes in the background, empathetic and calm, not harsh.

words.def: one single person, thought of separately from a group
words.note: Also an adjective: individual = separate, single. Opposite idea: society.
words.ex: Each individual has the right to express an opinion.
words.prompt: A row of grey faceless silhouette people, and among them one single colorful warm-toned person clearly standing out, softly highlighted by a warm circle of light.

words.def: a sudden good idea, or a person or thing that gives you one
words.note: Use: draw inspiration from something · be an inspiration to somebody.
words.ex: Her courage is an inspiration to us all.
words.prompt: A person sitting by a window looking at a warm sunrise over hills, a glowing lightbulb floating above the head, small sparkles, a pencil and notebook on the sill.

words.def: to stop someone while they are speaking or doing something
words.note: Root: inter (between) + rupt (break) → break into the middle.
words.ex: Sorry to interrupt, but there's a phone call for you.
words.prompt: Two people sitting and talking across a table, while a third person steps in between them raising one hand with an apologetic wave, clearly cutting into the conversation.

words.def: to keep several objects in the air; to handle several tasks at the same time
words.ex: She juggles a full-time job with raising three children.
words.prompt: A busy person juggling several objects in the air at once: a small laptop, a coffee cup, a folder and a phone, trying to keep them all up, slight comedic stress.

words.def: feeling bitter or angry about unfair treatment
words.note: Use: be resentful of / about something. Verb: resent.
words.ex: He felt resentful about the unfair treatment.
words.prompt: A person sitting with arms crossed and a small frown, a little dark grey rain cloud hovering just above the head with tiny lightning, sulky body language.

words.def: the usual fixed way you do things; a set of regular actions
words.note: Common: daily routine. Also an adjective: routine = regular.
words.ex: Exercise has become part of my daily routine.
words.prompt: A cozy morning routine flat lay on a wooden table seen from above: an alarm clock, a toothbrush and cup, a steaming coffee mug, a small potted plant and a pair of running shoes, soft morning light.

words.def: the feeling that you are good and worthy; confidence in yourself
words.ex: Praise from teachers can boost a child's self-esteem.
words.prompt: A person standing tall and confident in front of a mirror, one hand on the heart, the reflection in the mirror glowing warmly with a proud gentle smile, soft golden light.

words.def: in a way that feels awkward for the body or in a social situation
words.note: Build: un + comfort + able → uncomfortable → uncomfortably.
words.prompt: A person sitting stiffly and awkwardly on a chair that is clearly too small, in a stuffy warm room with a small fan nearby, one sweat drop on the temple, embarrassed tight smile.
